No matter where the sintering te mperature is 1150 oC, 1250 oC or 1350 oC, Ti-185 MAP alloy always has a higher relative density than Ti -185 EP alloy at the same sintering temperature as shown in Figure 1, which should be the main cause that Ti -185 MAP alloy has a better mechanical property compared with Ti-185 EP alloy
the yield strength and hardness of Ti-185 alloy augment with the increase of the relative sintered density of Ti-185 alloy, namely, with the decrease of the porosity volume fraction of Ti -185 alloy
which has a relationship with the fact that oxygen is deemed to α -stabilizing element and the oxygen content of Ti-185 EP alloy is greater than that of Ti-185 MAP alloy

It is also the important cause that Ti-185 MAP alloy with a less α phase has a higher mechanical property than Ti-185 EP alloy with a more α phase, which is supported by several researches that the α phase is a softer phase compared with β phase in titanium alloys.

Compared with Ti-185 EP, the fewer oxygen amount of Ti-185 MAP as shown in Table 2 means more fresh titanium particles and higher surface activity, which can benefit the sintering densification of Ti-185 MAP alloy.

In the dehydrogenation process between about 430 oC and 800 oC, releasing of hydrogen leads to significant shrinkage and high density of crystal lattice defects, H atoms in the dehydrogenation have the surface cleaning effects through reacting with oxygen in titanium and releasing the reaction product of water, which can accelerate the densification.
